items.title: King of Sparta: Who Was Leonidas?
items.description:
Who was the real Leonidas from the movie 300? In this podcast episode of the Ancients with Dr Andrew Bayliss and Tristan Hughes, they uncover the ancient historical figure of King Leonidas.

items.title: Arabella Hunt's True Love? Queer History at Hampton Court Palace
items.description:
Arabella Hunt was a famous singer and musician in the 17th Century. She married James Howard, but the marriage was annulled after only six months when Arabella sued for annulment, claiming that James was, in fact, a woman named Amy Poulter. 

This LGBTQ+ History Month, discover some of the queer lives and possibilities connected to our sites by listening to the Historic Royal Palaces podcast: https://open.spotify.com/episode/1ceE6uF3nrZOMJUD9t1Nae?si=ALWiOyQ4Tred7TcKJXLwXw

items.title: S2 Ep17: Buster Keaton, The Exclusive Property of MGM
items.description:
Famous for his dead-pan comedy style, Buster Keaton was one the kings of slapstick comedy. But behind his success hid battles with production studios, his wife, and his addiction. In today’s episode, we’re reading Keaton’s memoir “My Wonderful World of Slapstick”.

What does flavor really mean? And how does it work? In this episode, Joe visits a flavor chemistry lab to meet a master flavorist and uncover how taste, smell, sound, sight, and memory combine in the brain. Along the way, he learns how flavors are built molecule by molecule—and why identical foods can taste completely different to different people.

discovery_articles.title: Is This Giant Celestial Body a Moon, a Planet or Something in Between? The Strange Object Calls Astronomical Labels Into Question
discovery_articles.snippet: The newly found object, estimated to be roughly as massive as Jupiter, orbits a brown dwarf—a "failed star"—which in turn circles a small star. For now, researchers are calling the puzzling body an "exosatellite"
discovery_articles.ferns_note: A Jupiter-sized world orbiting a failed star that itself orbits a real star — it's a cosmic nesting doll that quietly breaks every category we thought we had for planets and moons. The universe, as ever, did not consult our textbooks.

discovery_articles.title: A Brief History of Hold Music, From Early Patents to the Soundtrack of Customer-Service Purgatory
discovery_articles.snippet: Sixty years ago, Alfred A. Levy patented his “telephone hold program system.” Little did he know a teenager’s unearthed New Age practice tape would become its enduring anthem
discovery_articles.ferns_note: The hold music most of us have seethed through for decades turns out to be a teenager's forgotten New Age practice tape, discovered almost by accident and somehow never dethroned. There's a melancholy poetry in the fact that our collective waiting soundtrack was never meant for us at all.

featured_read.title: How to Stop Waiting and Start Living: A Jolt from Henry James
featured_read.snippet: "It wouldn't have been failure to be bankrupt, dishonoured, pilloried, hanged; it was failure not to be anything."
featured_read.blurb: Henry James's sharpest line cuts straight to the quiet dread most of us carry: that the real catastrophe isn't losing, but the half-lived life spent waiting for conditions to be right. This one is worth reading slowly, with the lights low and your excuses set aside.
